 THIS CRP IS FILED UNDER SECTION 115 OF CPC AGAINST THE ORDER DATED 02.03.2022 PASSED ON IA No.3 IN O.S.No.800/2019 ON THE FILE OF THE ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND JMFC, DEVANAHALLI, REJECTING THE APPLICATION FILED UNDER ORDER 7 RULE 11(a)(b) AND (d)
OF CPC FOR REJECTION OF PLAINT.

THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR ADMISSION THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
This matter is listed for admission.

Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.1 and learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2.
2.

This CRP is filed under Section 115 of CPC against the order dated 02.03.2022 passed on I.A.No.3 in O.S.No.800/2019 on the file of the Additional Senior Civil Judge & JMFC., at Devanahalli,
dismissing the application filed under Order VII Rule 11 of CPC to reject the plaint.
Hence, this petition is filed before this Court.

The main contention of the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner before this Court is that the suit schedule property belongs to the petitioner and the relief sought in the plaint by the first respondent is for the relief of declaration to declare that he is the owner and in possession of the suit property.
The learned counsel would submit that the property was already acquired and the possession was taken and the compensation also paid and now he cannot seek for the relief of declaration.

The learned counsel also would vehemently contend that the sale transaction had taken place long back i.e., 53 years old transaction and after the lapse of 53 years, the suit is filed for the T A Narayanaswamy vs Sri T.N. Raghavendra on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158345901/
2 relief of declaration and not sought for any relief of possession since possession has already been taken.

sentences.text: The suit is also barred by limitation.
All these grounds are urged before the Trial Court when an application was filed under Order VII Rule 11 of CPC.
The learned counsel also would submit that the suit is also hit by Section 34 of the Specific Relief Act.
These are the aspects has not been considered by the Trial Court.

4. The learned counsel appearing for the respondents would vehemently contend that though several sale NC: 2023:KHC:21175 transactions have taken place, the respondent/plaintiff has purchased the property on 25.04.1966 to the extent of 0.24 guntas out of 1 acre 3 guntas.
Even if any sale deed is executed subsequent to 23.08.1966, the same will not confer any right to the extent of 0.24 guntas, which have already been sold in favour of the respondent.

The learned counsel also would vehemently contend that there is no dispute with regard to the property being acquired and the same is also stated in the plaint itself, but dispute is with regard to the disbursement of the compensation amount and the question of challenging the acquisition does not arise.
They are not challenging the acquisition and only challenged with regard to the title in respect of the property.

The Trial Court having considered the grounds urged in the application as well as in the objection statement rightly come to the conclusion that with regard to the limitation is concerned, the same is mixed question of facts and law and also there is a dispute with regard to the title, the same has to be adjudicated.
The Court has to consider the prior sale deed, which confers the right on this ground only the Trial Court rejected the application.
Hence, there are no grounds to NC: 2023:KHC:21175 entertain an application filed under Order VII Rule 11 of CPC to reject the plaint.
5. Having heard the respective counsel, while considering an application filed under Order VII Rule 11 of CPC, the Court has to consider the averments of the plaint.

The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would vehemently contend that in paragraph No.9, it is contended that the revision petitioners are strangers to the suit schedule property and they have no right, title or interest over the suit schedule property.

Again, i.e., on 01.10.2019, the defendants along with their henchmen tried to interfere with the suit schedule property, and when they are not in possession, the question of interfering does not arise.

Having taken note of the averments of the plaint and the Court while exercising the powers under Order VII Rule 11 of CPC has to consider the averments of the plaint and not the defense of the defendants.

It is also a settled law that the plaintiff's in the suit in paragraph No.4, they have pleaded how they acquired the property specifically mentioning that they have purchased the property vide Sale Deed dated 25.04.1966, and contended that based on the said Sale Deed, they are having title.

In paragraph No.7 contended NC: 2023:KHC:21175 that the third defendant acquired the suit schedule property for the purpose of industrial development and ready to disburse the compensation in favour of defendant Nos.1 and 2.
Hence, the suit is filed for the relief of declaration and for disbursal of the amount, which is in dispute.
Hence, specifically mentioned the same and not suppressed anything even acquisition of the property and only dispute is with regard to the title of the property.
The cause of action is also stated in paragraph No.10 with regard to when interference was made.
6. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners would vehemently contend that when the possession is not with them, the question of interference does not arise.

Whether they are having the possession or not once again a matter of trial and the same cannot be decided in an application filed T A Narayanaswamy vs Sri T.N. Raghavendra on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158345901/
3 under Order VII Rule 11 of CPC.

sentences.text: It is a settled law that the Court has to look into the averments of the plaint and not the defense.

The Trial Court having considered the material on record came to the conclusion that when the dispute is raised with regard to the suit is barred by law, the same is also mixed question of facts and law and the same cannot be decided under Order VII Rule 11 of CPC.
The Trial Court also while NC: 2023:KHC:21175 considering the grounds urged in the application, in detail discussed the grounds which have been urged in the application.

Now, the dispute is with regard to disbursal of the compensation amount and also taken note of the fact that the compensation was taken in respect of the undisputed portion of property and not taken compensation in respect of the disputed property.
When such being the case, the issue of title has to be decided in the said suit and the same cannot be adjudicated in an application filed under Order VII Rule 11 of CPC.
It is a settled law that the defense cannot be taken while considering the application filed under Order VII Rule 11 of CPC.

When the issue involved between the parties with regard to the title as well as disbursement of the amount and the Trial Court also taken note of the challenge, which is not made in respect of the acquisition, the dispute is with regard to the disbursement of the amount.

Hence, I do not find any error committed by the Trial Court and the matter requires to be tried before the Trial Court with regard to the title and disbursement of the amount in respect of the property which has been acquired.

There is no reference under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act to decide the issue involved between the parties with regard to NC:
2023:KHC:21175 the claim made by the plaintiff in respect of 24 guntas of land.
Under the circumstances, I do not find any error committed by the Trial Court in dismissing the application filed under Order VII Rule 11 of CPC.

This Court can direct the Trial Court to dispose of the matter within a stipulated period since the Trial Court could not dispose of the same in view of pendency of this revision petition though filed on time.

7. In view of the discussions made above, I pass the following:
ORDER (i) The Revision Petition is dismissed.

(ii) The Trial Court has fixed a period of nine months for conclusion of trial and in view of C.R.P. being pending before the Court and the same was not concluded, the Trial Court is directed to dispose of the matter within six months from today.
(iii) Both the counsel and their respective parties are directed to assist the Trial Court in disposal of the case within a stipulated time.
In view of dismissal of the petition, IA-1/2022 for stay does not survive for consideration, the same stands disposed of.
